ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA), particularly Part 12.1 (Registration of businesses performing money services), Part 1 and regulations including the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations (SOR/2002-184), and the Criminal Code, R.S.C., 1985, c. C-46, as amended for sanctions implementation; Quebec: Act respecting the legal publicity of sole proprietorships, partnerships and legal persons (Legal Publicity Act), CQLR c. P-45, which provides for a register of enterprises requiring disclosure of certain beneficial ownership information; Quebec Business Enterprises Act (Act respecting the Business Enterprises Registries), CQLr c. P-44.1 replaced the Legal Publicity Act regime for most enterprises; applicable AML/CFT supervision includes FINTRAC under PCMLTFA and the Quebec Financial Markets Authority (Autorité des marchés financiers, AMF) for certain sectors.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic screening must be conducted for all proposed partners and beneficial owners before registering a Quebec limited partnership. Screening requirements derive from the PCMLTFA obligations on reporting entities (financial institutions, money service businesses, accountants and lawyers in specified circumstances), FINTRAC guidance, and the United Nations Act, S.C. 2000, c.31, regulation lists implementing UN sanctions, and Canada's domestic sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act. The screening should include: 29.9% or greater direct/indirect beneficial ownership in a limited partnership triggers registry disclosure to the Quebec enterprise registrar (if the entity is a registrable entity); verification against Canadian Consolidated Sanctions List (OSSI), OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council sanctions lists, and PEP databases (including domestic provincial MPP positions); enhanced due diligence if the partner is a politically exposed person, a high-risk jurisdiction, or if the source of funds is not clear; and documentation of screening date, list version, matching hits and clearance rationale. Note that Quebec's registry does not publicly expose the UBO file; beneficial ownership is transmitted to the Quebec enterprise registrar and made accessible only to government bodies and certain authorized persons as provided by law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises – Registre des entreprises (Quebec Business Registry) online service at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; name reservation application available through the Registraire's service providers / certified transactional portal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11) and the Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business (CQLR c. C-11, r. 9), the name of the enterprise must be in French unless an exemption is granted. A distinctive part of the name may be in another language if accompanied by a generic French term (e.g., 'Hotpot' as a distinctive element plus 'Restaurant' or 'Inc.'); French characters and accents are mandatory unless expressly exempted. Transliteration of a foreign brand must be rendered in Latin characters with French orthographic conventions; a trademark registered in a foreign script may be used as the distinctive element if the other elements of the name are French and the foreign script is accompanied by the generic French descriptor.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Incorporation, Corporation, Limited, Limited Partnership, LLP, Inc., Ltee/Ltée (unless the entity is actually that form) – misleading corporate or partnership designations
'Québec' or 'Quebec' as part of the distinctive element in a manner suggesting government affiliation or territorial designation without authority

'Banque', 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Assurance', 'Insurance', 'Finance', 'Bursa', 'Stock exchange', 'University', 'College', 'Hospital', 'Chamber of Commerce', 'Government', 'Ministry', 'Office' – words requiring prior ministerial approval or prohibiting use where regulated
Words that induce error or contravene public order, good morals or statutory prohibitions under the Legal Publicity Act / Business Enterprises Act and the Charter of the French Language
References to a business that is not subject to Quebec law or that implies a legal personality or liability limitation not held by the limited partnership
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected by the Registraire des entreprises, the applicant may, within 60 days from the date of notification, file a written application for reconsideration or an administrative review with the Registraire des entreprises indicating the name clearance file number, grounds for the appeal, and a revised proposed name if desired. If the request is refused or is not answered within a reasonable time, a judicial review may be sought before the Superior Court of Quebec (Cour supérieure du Québec) in the judicial district of Quebec or Montreal, pursuant to the provisions of the Legal Publicity Act (CQLR c. P-45, ss. 97 and following) and the general administrative law remedies under the Code of Civil Procedure (art. 529 et seq. C.C.P.). It is also possible to submit a new name reservation request with amendments and additional supporting materials (consent letters from the holder of a prior name or trademark, or a certified trademark registration) without waiting for the appeal to be exhausted, to preserve the 30-day window. All communications must be submitted and processed through the Registraire's online services or in writing, in French unless a written waiver/authorization has been obtained.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Assessed as conditionally permissible for a limited partnership in the hotpot restaurant / condiment supply sector. A registered office in Quebec with a physical mailing address does not need to be the restaurant premises; however, to satisfy registrable entity rules and business licensing, the enterprise must maintain an accessible place in Quebec for service of process and records. For this industry, virtual office provided by licensed registered office service providers is generally accepted for registry compliance, since the partnership register does not require a commercial rug. Unannounced onsite inspections for a restaurant operator are risk-bearing and can be significant, because food safety/restaurant permits may require a physical presence of at least the establishment at the restaurant property, not the registered office. If the company employs staff or handles inventory, tax registration and QST/HST registrations may demand a more substantive address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections is assessed as 70-80% for the restaurant operations (due to public health inspections, municipal licensing, fire safety, alcohol/liquor licensing if applicable, and labour standards inspections) and 10-20% for the registered office itself under Quebec's registrant and tax compliance inspections. For the hotpot/condiment manufacturing sub-activity, public health food-processing facility inspections are mandatory and generally unannounced, with estimated 85-95% likelihood of at least one food safety inspection in the first 12 months of operation by the Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ) or local health authority for the restaurant dining area.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2236-2261 (societe en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 7-23 (declaration and registration requirements); Taxation Act, CQLR c. I-3, for fiscal registration of the partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ), a division of the Ministere de la Justice du Quebec; electronic filing through Registraire en ligne
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Declaration de societe en commandite) filed under s. 18 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a societe en commandite; partners' contributions are fixed in the partnership agreement, and limited partners' liability is capped at their agreed contribution (art. 2251 CCQ). No escrow account is mandated by provincial law; however, contributed funds should be held in a Canadian commercial bank account (preferably in Quebec) to satisfy bank KYC rules under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and Quebec tax allocation requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the general partner of the Limited Partnership, acting as its sole manager, hereby subscribes to its partnership interest under the Declaration of Limited Partnership to be filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is established at the address stated in said declaration; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed authorized representative to open banking accounts, execute restaurant leases and merchant acquiring agreements; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the general partner shall obtain licences from MAPAQ, municipal permits, and register for GST/QST and payroll accounts; RESOLVED FURTHER, that professional advisors be engaged to complete formation and regulatory compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Legal Availability Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Registraire en ligne portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an optional name reservation request through the REQ online service or request a certificate of non-registration to verify that the proposed limited partnership name is distinctive and not confusing with existing enterprise names in Quebec. For a societe en commandite, the name must include the expression 'societe en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.' (or 'L.P.'). Provide the general partner's identification (name, domicile, and, if a legal person, its registration number) and search the REQ database before drafting the declaration.
required_dossiers: Completed REQ name reservation form
Identification of proposed general partner (individual: driver's licence or passport; legal person: REQ or incorporation number)
Written authorization if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a fresh reservation with up to three alternative names, or submit a written representation to the REQ Direction de l'immatriculation within 30 days of the refusal seeking reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil-law notary or legal counsel acting for the partners; executed deed to be transmitted to REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Declaration of Limited Partnership under arts. 2236-2243 of the Civil Code of Quebec and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. The declaration must state the firm name, the object of the partnership, the address of the registered office in Quebec, the name and address of each general partner who assumes unlimited liability, and confirmation that at least one general partner is appointed to manage the partnership. Execute the declaration as a private deed unless the partners elect a notarial deed en minute. Every general partner must sign the declaration. The executed declaration must be filed with REQ within 60 days of the formation of the partnership.
required_dossiers: Declaration of Limited Partnership (duly signed by all general partners)
Partnership agreement (convention de societe en commandite) retained internally
Identification documents for all general partners
If a legal person is a general partner: extract from REQ registry or equivalent proof of registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a deficiency notice, submit a corrective amending declaration (declaration modificative) or rectify the original declaration within the cure period stated in the notice; failures may be cured by a fresh filing with payment of the prescribed late fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration (Immatriculation) with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Registraire en ligne or in-person service point
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Declaration of Limited Partnership electronically through Registraire en ligne or in person at a REQ service point. Pay the statutory registration fee (approximately CAD 85). Upon successful registration, REQ issues the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and a certificate of registration; the partnership acquires legal personality from the standpoint of civil publicity and its firm name is protected. This registration satisfies art. 2237 CCQ and the publicity obligations of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
required_dossiers: Executed Declaration of Limited Partnership
Payment of the registration fee
Contact and mailing information of the partnership
Mandate of the filing representative (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is rejected, file a corrected declaration with an explanatory letter; if the filing is late, effect registration upon payment of the late fee and interest; any interested person may apply to the Superior Court of Quebec to rectify or strike out inaccurate registry information.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Partnership Agreement, Internal Governance and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel (avocat or notaire) acting for the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the internal convention de societe en commandite covering capital contributions, profit and loss sharing, the management powers of the general partner, indemnification, withdrawal and retirement of partners, and dispute resolution. Although not filed with REQ, this agreement governs banking relationships, POS merchant acquiring, and tax allocation among partners. Adopt the pro-forma resolution of the general partner appointing the authorized representative and bank signatories. Maintain a physical registered office in Quebec for service of process and statutory notices.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement (convention de societe en commandite)
Pro-forma resolution of the general partner
Proof of registered office address (lease or letter of consent from the office provider)
KYC and beneficial ownership documents for banking and merchant acquiring
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Disputes among partners are resolved under the partnership agreement or by the Superior Court of Quebec; a defective registered office is regularized by filing a declaration of change of address with REQ without penalty if filed within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with Revenu Quebec and the Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Quebec (Registre d'inscription) and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ, register the limited partnership for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) under the Act respecting the Quebec sales tax and obtain a CRA business number (BN) with GST/HST, payroll (RC), and partnership (RT-1) accounts. Register once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 or voluntarily to claim input tax credits and input tax refunds. Identify the general partner responsible for the partnership's tax filings and provide Canadian banking details. Complete the reciprocal GST/QST self-assessment where required.
required_dossiers: REQ certificate of registration (NEQ)
Completed Revenu Quebec LM-1 registration form or online registration request
CRA RC165 (or RC159 for GST/HST) registration documents
Partnership agreement and percentage allocation of income and loss for each partner
Identification of the tax representative if a general partner is non-resident
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed or queried, contact Revenu Quebec's business registration service to complete the file; late registration is generally effective as of the date of the request, and failure to register may attract penalties under the QSTA, which can be mitigated by filing the signed LM-1 with supporting documents and a written explanation of reasonable cause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Zoning Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City or local municipality (e.g., Ville de Montreal - Service des permis d'affaires)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence (permis d'entreprise) for a full-service restaurant, submitting the REQ registration certificate, a certified copy of the lease, a zoning attestation, and the proposed special occupancy. Verify that the premises are zoned for commercial food service and that signage conforms to the municipal by-law. Pay the annual licence fee and display the certificate on the premises. This municipal clearance is a precondition for opening the hotpot restaurant to the public.
required_dossiers: REQ certificate of registration (NEQ)
Lease or proof of premises ownership
Zoning attestation from the municipal planning department
Completed municipal business licence application and fee schedule
Copy of the MAPAQ food establishment permit application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence is refused on zoning grounds, request a conditional permit, apply to the municipal committee of adjustment (comite consultatif d'urbanisme or equivalent) for a minor variance, or appeal the decision within the appeal period stated in the written refusal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministere de l'Agriculture, des Pecheries et de l'Alimentation du Quebec (MAPAQ) - Direction du controle des aliments
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permis d'exploitation d'un etablissement alimentaire (Food Establishment Permit) - Restaurant, Food Service and Food Court category

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) together with the municipal sewer authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration level (non-ESI) - light commercial food service installation subject to municipal wastewater by-laws and the Reglement sur la qualite de l'atmosphere; a full EIA report is not required unless kitchen ventilation grease emissions or wastewater volumes exceed municipal thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Kitchen effluent must pass through a certified grease interceptor before sanitary sewer discharge; wastewater BOD5 and TSS must not exceed 300 mg/L each (or stricter municipal by-law limits); ventilation exhaust must meet municipal odour and VOC limits with grease filters and hoods maintained per NFPA 96 cleaning schedules; waste cooking oil, grease and organic residues must be recovered by a licensed transporter under the Reglement sur les matieres residuelles.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification required under the Regime de securite incendie: approved fire extinguishers, a UL/NFPA 96 hood suppression system, emergency exits and evacuation signage verified by the local fire service; building occupancy certificate and structural load verification of kitchen equipment, mezzanine or ventilation supports by a professional engineer where required; CNESST establishment registration and occupational health and safety compliance for hot oil handling, slip-resistant flooring, and work equipment prior to opening.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Agence du revenu du Canada); GST/HST and income-tax portal: CRA My Business Account at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-account.html. In Quebec, since 1 October 2017, Revenu Québec administers both the federal GST and the provincial QST under the CRA-Revenu Québec GST/HST administration agreement; Revenu Québec business portal: Clé numérique d'affaires at https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The general partner applies to the CRA for a nine-digit Business Number (BN) using Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number), or through CRA My Business Account; a non-resident applicant uses the non-resident registration path and must establish that it carries on business in Canada. Step 2: Register the BN GST/HST RT program account with CRA; for Quebec, register the limited partnership and each general partner with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the NEQ (Québec enterprise number) and file the declaration of registration of a limited partnership within 60 days of opening an establishment. Step 3: File the Revenu Québec registration declaration for the GST/HST/QST system (Quebec form LM-1-V, Application for Registration under the GST/HST and QST System) to open the QST TQ program account, thereby obtaining a Revenu Québec reference number of the form RP followed by six digits. Step 4: A foreign limited partnership must designate a representative for service of process in Quebec and provide the extra-provincial registration certificate; certificates of registration and account numbers are issued immediately by both portals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: For Canadian federal income tax and Quebec income tax, the limited partnership is fiscally transparent under section 96 of the Income Tax Act, with each partner reporting its share of partnership income or loss on its own return and no entity-level income tax being imposed on the LP. However, for GST/HST and QST purposes, the partnership is itself a distinct person that must register, collect, and remit; it is not eligible for treatment as a tax-exempt zone entity. Territorial scope: a Canadian-resident partner is taxed on worldwide income, whereas a non-resident partner is taxed only on Canadian-source and Quebec-source income, subject to Part XIII withholding rules on certain payments from the partnership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None equivalent to a US check-the-box election exists in Canada; entity classification follows the common law and statutory characterization, and the LP remains transparent for income tax while being a separate person for GST/HST and QST. Available elections relevant to this structure include: (i) a partnership fiscal-period election under section 249.1 of the Income Tax Act permitting a non-calendar year-end where all partners elect and conditions are met; (ii) an elective rollover of property transferred to the partnership under subsection 97(2) of the Income Tax Act; (iii) a partnership capital cost allowance election under subsection 96(2.1) of the Income Tax Act; (iv) the GST/HST Quick Method election under section 220 of the Excise Tax Act and its QST counterpart, allowing a restaurant operator to remit using a reduced percentage of taxable sales; and (v) voluntary GST/HST and QST registration by a small supplier with turnover below CAD 30,000. Canada's hybrid-mismatch measures provide no protective entity-classification election for a non-resident limited partnership; every cross-border payment must be tested on its facts against the transfer-pricing rules of section 247 and the general anti-avoidance rule of section 245 of the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / harmonized sales tax) administered federally by the CRA and, within Quebec, by Revenu Québec, applied jointly with the Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ); restaurant dine-in meal sales and sales of prepared heated food for off-premises consumption are standard-rated supplies, while exported condiment goods are zero-rated supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: A person whose worldwide tax-inclusive revenues from taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over the four preceding consecutive calendar quarters ceases to be a small supplier and must register for GST/HST; the same CAD 30,000 threshold applies for QST registration. For this hotpot restaurant operation in Quebec, registration is mandatory immediately upon commencement of business because the direct-operated dining premises constitute a permanent establishment, billing through POS merchant acquiring generates taxable supplies in Quebec from the first day, and projected annual turnover will far exceed the small-supplier threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec impose no real-time fiscal clearance, no fiscal memory or cryptographic stamping requirement, no continuous-control SAF-T mandate, and no government-API invoice certification scheme. Electronic invoicing is permitted and interoperable through the Peppol network on a voluntary basis; mandatory electronic filing applies once annual taxable turnover exceeds CAD 1.5 million, requiring GST/HST returns via GST/HST NETFILE or an approved EDI channel and, for QST, requiring returns transmitted electronically through Revenu Québec's Transmission électronique service. A restaurant's POS system need not be government certified; however, each invoice or simplified point-of-sale receipt issued in Quebec must show the registrant name, the nine-digit BN, the GST rate and amount, and the QST rate and amount, and records must be retained for six years. Revenu Québec may cross-check reported sales data against payment-card and merchant-acquirer aggregate data, and it has expressly flagged the restaurant sector for electronic-receipt verification.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating applies to the condiment-supply component only where the Quebec limited partnership supplies packaged sauces and food condiments for export and the goods are shipped directly by the supplier out of Canada, with title passing to the non-resident purchaser outside Canada, or where the goods are delivered to a common carrier for export at the point of exit; the governing authority is Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, in particular section 5 for exported goods, and the parallel QST zero-rating rules. Services that are reasonably regarded as ancillary to the exported goods, such as handling, storage, and transport performed in Canada for the exported property, are also zero-rated. Dine-in hotpot meal sales and sales of prepared or heated meals for take-away are standard-rated supplies in Quebec at the combined 14.975% rate; the take-away exemption for basic groceries is unavailable where the food is supplied heated, pre-cooked, or packaged as a meal ready for consumption. To substantiate the zero-rating of exported condiments, the LP must obtain from the non-resident customer a written purchase order, shipping instructions, transport documentation, and evidence of foreign-currency settlement; the LP must also hold a CBSA export declaration confirming the actual departure from Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A, filed electronically with the Canada Border Services Agency through the Canadian Export Reporting System or the Canadian Integrated Export Declaration portal for shipments over CAD 2,000 or of controlled goods)
Commercial Invoice stating complete HTS classification, country of origin, unit prices, and total export value
Bill of Lading or airway waybill showing carrier name, voyage or flight number, port of exit, and foreign destination
CBSA approved export-report confirmation number evidencing the electronic export declaration
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MT103 credit evidence linking foreign-currency settlement to the exporting LP's bank account
Packing list and container or shipment tracking records showing the goods physically left Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Excise Tax Act imposes a false-statement or omission penalty of not less than CAD 250 and 25% of the denied refund or of the excess of reported tax, and Revenu Québec applies equivalent penalties under the Act respecting the Quebec sales tax for false declarations and omissions. CRA may reassess GST/HST net tax and any rebate within four years, without time limit in the case of misrepresentation, fraud, or failure to file, and Revenu Québec mirrors this reassessment power for QST. Interest on arrears accrues daily and the penalty rate is materially higher for repeat or deliberate non-compliance. For deliberate evasion, fines reach 200% of the tax sought to be evaded, with terms of imprisonment available on conviction. Export zero-rating claims are subjected to intensive audit scrutiny through CBSA export-data matching, carrier shipping logs, warehouse records, and foreign-bank remittance tracing; although the ETA does not codify a 180-day repatriation rule, CRA administrative practice expects export proceeds to be received within the 180-day benchmark, and failure to demonstrate timely repatriation, absent documented commercial reasons, triggers transfer-pricing review under section 247 of the Income Tax Act, deemed-receipt recharacterization, clawback of all input tax credits previously recovered on the zero-rated supply chain, denial of future zero-rating, and cumulative penalties and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), Ottawa; exchange-control policy is functionally distributed between the Department of Finance Canada (currency sovereignty and sanctions), OSFI (prudential supervision of Schedule I/II banks), FINTRAC (cross-border transaction reporting under the PCMLTFA), and the Investment Canada Act directorate (foreign-investment review). Canada operates a free-floating currency regime and has had no dedicated foreign-exchange-control authority since the Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1952.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts without licensing, quotas, prior central-bank approval, or end-use restrictions. Profit distributions from a Quebec limited partnership (Civil Code of Quebec arts. 2236-2255) to resident and non-resident partners are unrestricted; the only frictions are Income Tax Act Part XIII withholding for non-resident partners (15%-25% treaty-dependent) and CRS/FATCA self-certification obligations, not exchange-control clearance. The binding convertibility constraint for the overseas direct-operated hotpot chain lies in the host jurisdiction (e.g., onshore RMB capital controls in China or other emerging-market restrictions), not in Canada. To smooth repatriation and bank source-of-funds validation, the LP should maintain audited financial statements, CRA and Revenu Quebec tax-clearance certificates, and transfer-pricing documentation for the condiment supply line.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline on export proceeds, service income, or intercompany trade receipts. Export earnings from condiment and equipment sales to the overseas restaurant may be retained offshore indefinitely in any convertible currency. The only obligations are (a) arm's-length pricing and contemporaneous documentation under Income Tax Act s. 247 for related-party exports, (b) FINTRAC reporting of electronic fund transfers and large cash transactions at the CAD 10,000 threshold, and (c) CBSA export declarations for goods above the low-value threshold. Treasury design should centralize USD export collections in a Schedule I bank account under the Quebec LP and convert via natural payroll/purchase cycles to minimize FX drag.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency CAD/USD with GST/QST settlement and cash sweep)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Federation des caisses Desjardins du Quebec
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (POS merchant acquiring and daily cash-cycle management)
Capital Escrow Account (construction fit-out escrow and USD corridor via BMO Harris)
Operational Account (cross-border SWIFT and trade disbursements)
Operational Account (restaurant merchant services and liquidity sweeps)
Capital Escrow Account (Asia-Pacific and cross-border trade corridor)
Capital Escrow Account (Quebec SME leasing and security deposits)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary banking rail; viable only as a supplementary payment layer. Canada does not recognize 'electronic money institution' as a licensed category; foreign EMI licences (FCA/EMD2) confer no passporting rights into Canada, and only chartered banks may take deposits under the Bank Act. A FINTRAC-registered money services business (MSB) or payment fintech (e.g., Wise, Convera, Corpay) may legally provide cross-border payments and multi-currency wallets without deposit-taking, but cannot hold CDIC-insured balances, issue import letters of credit, or provide Payments Canada Lynx membership. Recommended architecture: retain capital escrow and core operating accounts at a Schedule I bank; use a FINTRAC MSB only for low-value trade disbursements and FX conversions below CAD 25,000 per transaction, subject to dual-control approval and monthly reconciliation against the main ledger.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical appearance of at least one authorized signatory (director or authorized officer of the corporate general partner) is de facto mandatory for the initial account opening at all major Quebec branches. Remote video onboarding is offered only to low-risk domestic clients and still requires a notarized certified true copy of the signatory's ID, a certified copy of the general partner's constating documents and resolution, and a fresh declaration of partnership (declaration de societe en commandite) issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec within the preceding 30 days. If all partners or GP officers are non-resident, banks generally require either an in-person identity attestation at a Canadian embassy/consulate or the appointment of a Quebec-resident attorney-in-fact, plus enhanced due diligence under OSFI Guidance E-13. There is no Quebec statutory mandate for in-person appearance; the requirement derives solely from bank risk-based KYC policy applicable to partner-owned investment vehicles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: non-resident limited partners owning 25% or more with an incomplete or nominee-tainted ownership chain, or through a shell jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (1) full beneficial-ownership chart down to all natural persons; (2) Revenu Quebec enterprise-register extract evidencing the Law 25 beneficial-ownership declaration; (3) FATCA/CRS self-certifications (W-8BEN-E / W-8IMY / CRS forms) for every 25%+ UBO; (4) the limited partnership agreement with the capital-account schedule; (5) a written undertaking to re-file the registry within 30 days of any ownership change; (6) notarized declarations of identity for each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth insufficiency: unexplained lump-sum capital injection into escrow or operating accounts from untraced investor accounts or cryptocurrency conversions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce: (1) 6-12 months of originating bank statements from each contributing partner; (2) CRA notices of assessment and Revenu Quebec tax clearance for the contributing partners; (3) audited financial statements or certified net-worth statements; (4) signed capital-contribution certificates linking each wire to a specific LP subscription; (5) a written source-of-wealth/source-of-funds narrative with an express covenant prohibiting crypto-derived contributions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-heavy hospitality exposure: overseas restaurants operating on high cash acceptance, creating money-laundering red flags and triggering FINTRAC LCTR expectations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) integrated POS architecture showing centralized settlement; (2) cash-management and anti-structuring policy with daily deposit limits, dual custody, and reconciliation; (3) written tipping-policy documentation aligned with Quebec employment law; (4) FINTRAC LCTR/EFT reporting protocol with a named AML compliance officer; (5) internal audit trail for store-level cash-to-bank movement and variance review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade mismatch on the condiment supply line: SWIFT remittance details inconsistent with customs declarations, or invoices without transport evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble: (1) supply contracts with the overseas restaurant vehicle; (2) commercial invoices, packing lists, and HS-consistent classification for hotpot condiments (HS 2103.90 / 0902); (3) bills of lading/air waybills and CBSA export declarations; (4) destination-country import filings; (5) cargo insurance certificates and warehouse receipts; (6) LC or MT103 records referencing identical invoice and purchase-order numbers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP screening triggers: jurisdiction or UBO flagged on OSFI/Global Affairs Canada consolidated lists, or a PEP in the overseas host country.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execute: (1) real-time sanctions and PEP screening of all UBOs and counterparties; (2) a written legal opinion confirming no OSFI/UN/EU/OFAC nexus; (3) an enhanced ongoing-monitoring agreement with quarterly transaction reviews; (4) corporate authorization resolutions in English and French; (5) documentation demonstrating the LP's exclusively commercial food-service purpose with no sanctioned-sector exposure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Step-wise compliant structure under the Quebec LP: (1) the general partner issues subscription notices allocating definitive capital-account commitments; (2) each partner sends a SWIFT MT103 to the designated Schedule I operating account in Quebec, with field 70 quoting the LP's Quebec enterprise registration number (NEQ) and the contribution certificate reference; (3) no Canadian exchange-control approval is required; FINTRAC EFT reporting applies at CAD 10,000 per cross-border transaction and is auto-filed by the bank; (4) where the contributing partner's source country imposes outbound exchange controls, the LP must obtain certified copies of that jurisdiction's administrative approvals prior to the wire; (5) incoming funds are converted only through the bank's designated FX facility and are held in a dedicated capital escrow sub-account pending project drawdown; (6) maintain a minimum liquidity buffer equal to 10% of quarterly CAPEX using a zero-balance-account structure to eliminate idle balances.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Recommended dual-rail framework: (A) Trade settlements - SWIFT MT103 direct credits for open-account supplier, payroll, and logistics payments, using field 71A 'OUR' and a structured remittance reference (invoice number plus destination customs code); (B) Documentary trade - commercial letters of credit issued on MT700 from the Canadian issuing bank to the overseas beneficiary bank for high-value fit-out and kitchen equipment; standby LC on MT760 to underpin premises leases; documentary collections (MT400/MT410) for first-time suppliers in restricted FX jurisdictions. For CAD-denominated same-day clearing use Payments Canada Lynx (RTGS) between bank treasury and the LP; retail POS settlement flows overnight through ACSS. All cross-border disbursements above CAD 10,000 are subject to FINTRAC EFT reporting, and physical exports require CBSA export declarations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/CNH; tenors 1-24 months) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or Canadian Master Agreement executed with the primary Schedule I bank; no regulatory pre-clearance required.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on non-convertible or capital-controlled host currencies (e.g., onshore CNY) referencing an agreed benchmark fix, with settlement in CAD or USD and documentation under ISDA FX definitions.
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD and CAD/CNH) matching the LP's long-term equity funding against overseas restaurant CAPEX, collateralized by cash margin or a bank-backed credit line.

Plain-vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars settled in CAD for condiment-export and profit-repatriation flows, subject to the bank's counterparty credit limit and hedge-effectiveness documentation.
FX swaps (simultaneous spot and forward trades) for liquidity reshuffling between the Quebec treasury account and the overseas operating entity without altering net FX exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) — Registraire des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the date of initial registration of the limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing constitutes an offence under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; two consecutive unfiled annual declarations expose the enterprise to cancellation or administrative strike-off by REQ, with resulting loss of registered legal publicity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the end of the LP's fiscal period; for a calendar-year fiscal period, by June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day up to a maximum of CAD 2,500, plus additional CRA compliance penalties for continued failure; no direct LP strike-off, but the CRA may pursue the general partner for enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the end of the LP's fiscal period; for a calendar-year fiscal period, by June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties and interest imposed by Revenu Québec under the Taxation Act for failure to file; repeated non-compliance exposes the general partner to provincial enforcement action and may impair the LP's good standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: There is no revenue-based statutory audit threshold for a private Quebec société en commandite. An independent audit is required if the partnership agreement or an unanimous partner resolution compels it, if the LP is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities legislation, or if the corporate general partner must consolidate the LP within audited financial statements. Otherwise, annual financial statements may be prepared without audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP applied under the CPA Canada Handbook; a private limited partnership may select Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). IFRS is mandatorily applicable if the LP is publicly accountable or if voluntarily elected.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Quebec LP has no share capital, so every transfer of a partnership interest is recorded in the register of partners and the register of ultimate beneficial owners. The general partner must file an REQ amendment within 30 days of any interest transfer, and each annual declaration must confirm that ultimate beneficial owner information is current and complete. Partners with direct or indirect control of 25% or more of the LP are treated as ultimate beneficial owners and must be disclosed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (names, contributions, profit-share percentages)
Register of Transfers of Partnership Interests
Minute Book of Partner and General Partner Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$200–US$500 per annum for a Quebec registered office/agent service that includes annual-declaration monitoring
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,000–US$7,000 for a single-location restaurant LP financial statement review; US$8,000–US$15,000 for a full independent audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: A Quebec limited partnership is generally a fiscally transparent partnership, not a corporation subject to federal or Quebec corporate income tax on its partnership income. For comparison, the general combined corporate income tax rate for an ordinary corporation carrying on business in Quebec is generally 26.5% (15% federal plus 11.5% Quebec), subject to eligibility, income type, and special rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The partnership itself generally claims no corporate tax holiday or corporate preferential deduction. Taxable income and permitted losses are generally allocated to partners under the partnership agreement and applicable tax rules. Each partner applies its own tax rates, deductions, credits, and treaty entitlements. A partner's ability to deduct a partnership loss may be limited, including by the at-risk rules applicable to limited partners.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Not applicable to the partnership as a separate corporate taxpayer. A partner's allocated non-capital loss is generally subject to that partner's applicable carryforward rules; for a Canadian corporation, the general period is 20 years forward and 3 years back, not 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013, Partnership Information Return, filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), generally electronically where electronic filing is required. Quebec: TP-600-V, Partnership Information Return, filed with Revenu Québec through its prescribed electronic services where electronic filing is required. Partners receive applicable T5013 and Quebec partnership slips, including RL-15 where required. A partnership return is an information return; it is not a corporate T2 income tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, for each partnership fiscal period. Separate GST/HST and QST returns may also be required at their applicable reporting frequencies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Federal T5013 and partner slips are generally due within 5 months after the end of the partnership fiscal period. Quebec TP-600-V and applicable partner slips are generally due within 5 months after the end of the fiscal period. Confirm any special deadline applying to the partnership's circumstances and filing method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013: Partnership identification and fiscal-period information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the partnership's legal name, business number, address, fiscal-period beginning and ending dates, partnership type, and other requested identification details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the partnership's Canadian business number and Canadian fiscal-period dates. Identify non-resident partners accurately and retain their country of residence, tax identification information, and ownership or profit-allocation records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013: Partnership income and expense schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report income, expenses, and required tax adjustments by applicable source and category; reconcile accounting results to amounts calculated under the Income Tax Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify income by source and character, including Canadian business income, rental income, interest, dividends, and royalties where applicable. Do not treat a non-resident partner's allocation as exempt merely because the partner is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013: Partner identification and allocation schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify each partner and report the partner's allocated income, deductions, credits, capital, and other reportable amounts using the prescribed schedules and slips.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide complete non-resident partner details and report allocations consistently with the partnership agreement and tax records. Assess Canadian filing, withholding, and treaty-documentation obligations separately for each partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: TP-600-V: Partnership identification and financial information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the partnership's identification, fiscal period, Quebec-source and other relevant income, expenses, and tax information under Quebec requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Quebec-source income and allocations accurately and identify non-resident partners as required. A federal filing or treaty claim does not replace the Quebec information return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issue and file applicable Quebec partnership slips reporting each partner's allocated income and other prescribed amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the prescribed partner status and identification information. Review whether allocated amounts are subject to Quebec tax, withholding, or a partner-level filing obligation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal late or deficient partnership-information-return penalties can include a daily penalty, generally $25 per day subject to a minimum and maximum, with higher penalties possible for specified failures, omissions, or knowing or grossly negligent false statements. Quebec may impose separate late-filing and information-return penalties and interest. The amount depends on the contravention and applicable statutory provisions; confirm current CRA and Revenu Québec assessments and electronic-filing requirements.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Not applicable to a partnership allocation: an LP does not ordinarily distribute corporate dividends. A payment by a Canadian corporation to a non-resident shareholder is generally subject to 25% Part XIII withholding tax, potentially reduced by an applicable income tax treaty if the recipient qualifies and procedural requirements are met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Determine the recipient's beneficial ownership, residence, income characterization, and eligibility under the applicable Canada tax treaty. Obtain a valid tax-residence certificate and prescribed treaty-benefit documentation, generally including CRA Form NR301 for a non-resident beneficial owner or the applicable alternative form, before applying a reduced withholding rate. Retain supporting evidence, apply the rate only when reasonable due diligence supports entitlement, remit and report withholding as required, and reassess when circumstances change. Treaty relief does not automatically eliminate Canadian tax on a non-resident partner's Canadian-source business income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Part XIII withholding is generally 25% on Canadian-source royalties and on interest paid or credited to a non-resident, subject to statutory exemptions and treaty reductions. Qualifying arm's-length interest is generally exempt under domestic law, subject to exceptions; related-party interest may remain taxable. Treaty rates vary by treaty, recipient, beneficial ownership, and payment classification. Payments for services performed in Canada can trigger separate Regulation 105 withholding, generally 15% of gross payments, subject to waiver or reduction procedures.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada has no general monetary threshold that relieves a taxpayer from the Income Tax Act section 247 contemporaneous-documentation requirement for reportable non-arm's-length cross-border transactions. The principal transfer-pricing penalty threshold generally concerns a net transfer-pricing adjustment exceeding the lesser of CAD 5 million and 10% of the taxpayer's gross revenue, subject to statutory conditions. Canadian law does not impose a universal OECD-style Local File and Master File filing threshold; Country-by-Country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups meeting the CAD 1 billion consolidated-revenue threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a general United Arab Emirates-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Canadian tax results remain subject to transfer-pricing rules, the general anti-avoidance rule, specific anti-avoidance provisions, beneficial-ownership requirements, and applicable substance-over-form and sham principles. Quebec may apply its own interpretive and anti-avoidance rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file partnership information returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file required federal T5013 or Quebec TP-600-V returns or partner slips by the applicable deadline, or filing materially incomplete or inaccurate information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Federal and Quebec late-filing, information-return, and false-statement penalties may apply, together with interest or other statutory consequences. Penalties depend on the specific failure, duration, and applicable provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: An LP has no directors solely by virtue of its partnership form. General partners and responsible persons may face statutory assessment or collection exposure where legislation applies; limited-partner status does not protect a person from liability for that person's own acts or from liabilities arising where the person is legally treated as a general partner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify non-resident partners, incorrectly treating Canadian-source income as exempt, or failing to withhold, remit, or report tax on payments subject to Part XIII or Regulation 105.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer or other responsible withholding agent may be assessed for unremitted tax, interest, and applicable penalties. Treaty relief is not available solely on the basis of a partner's non-resident status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where a corporation is the withholding agent, directors may be personally liable for specified unremitted source deductions under statutory director-liability rules, subject to statutory defences and due-diligence requirements. An LP's general partner and responsible persons require a fact-specific liability analysis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing cross-border non-arm's-length transactions outside the arm's-length standard, failing to maintain required contemporaneous documentation, or making materially inaccurate transfer-pricing representations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA may adjust income under section 247, assess consequential tax and interest, and impose a transfer-pricing penalty when statutory conditions and thresholds are met. Reassessment periods may be extended in specified circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Transfer-pricing adjustments are generally assessed against the taxpayer. Directors are not automatically personally liable for corporate tax solely because of an adjustment, but separate statutory, fraud, misrepresentation, or unremitted-withholding liabilities may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion, false books, or fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly concealing sales, fabricating expenses, maintaining false records, or making false or deceptive tax statements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Federal and Quebec tax statutes provide civil penalties, reassessment, interest, and criminal prosecution. Criminal convictions can result in substantial fines and imprisonment; the precise sanction depends on the charge and facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who authorize, participate in, or counsel an offence may face personal criminal liability. Civil tax liability does not automatically pierce the partnership or corporate veil; statutory liability and the individual's conduct must be assessed separately.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Representing an arrangement as an LP without satisfying Quebec partnership-law requirements, allowing a limited partner to act beyond legally protected limits, or mischaracterizing distributions as deductible expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential consequences include reclassification, denial of deductions or treaty benefits, reassessment, interest, penalties, and exposure under applicable Quebec partnership and civil-liability rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A limited partner may lose limited-liability protection to the extent provided by applicable law and the facts. The general partner ordinarily bears responsibility for partnership obligations; the precise exposure depends on the legal form, conduct, guarantees, and governing law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly dealing with proceeds of crime, structuring transactions to conceal ownership or source of funds, or making false statements to financial institutions or reporting entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Code and applicable proceeds-of-crime legislation may provide for asset restraint or forfeiture, fines, and imprisonment. Reporting and recordkeeping duties depend on whether the person or business is a regulated reporting entity and on the transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who knowingly participate, direct, or facilitate prohibited conduct may face personal criminal liability. A restaurant or LP is not automatically a reporting entity for every AML obligation; applicability depends on the activity and statutory classification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register, collect, report, or remit applicable GST/HST or QST, or failing to deduct and remit payroll source deductions for employees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA and Revenu Québec may assess tax, interest, late-remittance penalties, and other statutory penalties. Separate restaurant licensing, employment, and recordkeeping obligations may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a corporate employer or registrant may be personally liable for specified unremitted source deductions or sales taxes under applicable statutory provisions, subject to statutory defences. LP liability must be assessed by reference to the general partner, responsible persons, and the specific statute.
